text:
What to do:

  1. Choose your fairy-tale event. There are some ideas here (or you can choose your own):
    • A wolf has been roaming the streets and blowing down pigs’ houses!
    • An enormous beanstalk was suddenly found growing in Jack’s garden!
    • Wedding of the Century – Cinderella and Prince Charming are getting married!
    • Porridge stolen and house wrecked by mysterious golden-haired girl!
  2. On a piece of paper, make a mind-map to sort out your ideas – write your topic in the centre and your ideas around it.
  3. Decide on your opening sentence – it needs to be something that grabs the attention of the people watching/listening and tells them what the story will be about, for instance, “This morning, passers-by discovered an enormous beanstalk growing in Jack’s front garden.”
  4. Think about what order to include the ideas from your mind map.
  5. Decide on your closing sentence – it needs to be something that reminds people what the news story was about and why it was important.
  6. Make notes to help you remember what to say – you don’t necessarily need to write out all the words, just enough so you don’t forget anything!
  7. Present your news report – you could use someone in your house as your audience, video call someone you know, or film it!

For this activity, you need to imagine you are presenting the news on the TV or radio.
You will be presenting one news story in particular – an event from a fairy-tale!
